AccelFieldLoad: A static acceleration load that varies over the model.
AccelNodeLoad: A static acceleration load on individual grid points.
AcousticAbsorber: A frequency-dependent acoustic absorber element on the fluid-structure boundary.
AcousticAbsorberBrickProp: The property of an AcousticAbsorberHexa acoustic absorber element.
AcousticAbsorberHexa: An acoustic absorber element, a brick of the coupled fluid-structure analysis.
AcousticAbsorberProp: The property of an AcousticAbsorber frequency-dependent acoustic absorber element.
AcousticAxisymFluid2: An axisymmetric fluid element that connects two fluid points (the fluid of an axisymmetric slot or cavity analysis, together with an AcousticSlotControl card).
AcousticAxisymFluid3: An axisymmetric fluid element that connects three fluid points (the fluid of an axisymmetric slot or cavity analysis, together with an AcousticSlotControl card).
AcousticAxisymFluid4: An axisymmetric fluid element that connects four fluid points (the fluid of an axisymmetric slot or cavity analysis, together with an AcousticSlotControl card).
AcousticBarrierHexa: An acoustic barrier element, a brick of the coupled fluid-structure analysis.
AcousticBarrierProp: The property of an AcousticBarrierHexa acoustic barrier element.
AcousticInfiniteParams: Supplies named settings for acoustic infinite elements, including geometric tolerance and the starting number for additional points.
AcousticInfiniteProp: The property of the acoustic conjugate infinite elements (AcousticInfiniteTria3 and AcousticInfiniteQuad4).
AcousticInfiniteQuad4: The base of an acoustic conjugate infinite element, a quadrilateral of four acoustic grid points.
AcousticInfiniteTria3: The base of an acoustic conjugate infinite element, a triangle of three acoustic grid points.
AcousticPressureLoadMatrices: Identifies exported acoustic pressure-load matrices to use in a frequency-response model.
AcousticSlot3: A three-point slot element of the acoustic cavity analysis (an evenly spaced radial slot that solves the wave equation in two dimensions).
AcousticSlot4: A four-point slot element of the acoustic cavity analysis (an evenly spaced radial slot that solves the wave equation in two dimensions).
AcousticSlotBoundary: The list of the AcousticSlotSurfacePoint slot points on the boundary of a slot cavity with the axisymmetric fluid cavity.
AcousticSlotControl: Defines the harmonic index and default fluid properties for an acoustic cavity represented by slots.
AcousticSlotFluidPoint: An axisymmetric fluid point of the acoustic cavity (slot) analysis, a scalar degree of freedom (the pressure) with a two-dimensional location.
AcousticSlotSurfacePoint: A slot surface point of the acoustic cavity (slot) analysis, a scalar degree of freedom (the pressure) with a two-dimensional location and a slot width.
AcousticSourceLoad: An acoustic source given as power against frequency.
AdaptiveRefineControl: The control of the local adaptive mesh refinement for one criterion.
AdaptiveRefineCriterion: A criterion that picks the elements to refine in the adaptive mesh refinement.
AeroBeamSpline2: A beam spline, a line along which the structure bends and twists, that carries the displacements of a set of structural grid points to a row of aerodynamic boxes (or the elements of a body) and the forces back.
AeroBeamSpline5: A beam spline like AeroBeamSpline2, for any aerodynamic geometry: the points it moves are listed in an AeroBoxList instead of being a run of box numbers.
AeroBody2: An aerodynamic body (a slender body surrounded by an interference tube) for the Doublet-Lattice method, given by its leading point and its length.
AeroBodyProp2: The cross section of the AeroBody2 bodies that name it, and the angles at which the interference elements receive.
AeroBoxList: A list of aerodynamic boxes (or aerodynamic grid points) that an AeroControlSurface, an AeroComponent or an AeroSurfaceSpline4 or AeroBeamSpline5 names by its set ID.
AeroComponent: A component of the aerodynamic or structural model that a monitor point (MonitorIntegratedLoad1, MonitorDisplacement) or an external spline integrates over.
AeroComponentUnion: A component that is the union of other components.
AeroControlSchedule: The schedule of a control surface, its deflection as a function of the Mach number and the angle of attack, for a trim.
AeroControlSurface: An aerodynamic control surface, a variable of the trim that rotates up to two groups of aerodynamic boxes about their hinge lines.
AeroControlSurfaceNodes: The structural grid points that belong to a control surface, whose mass gives the moment of inertia of the surface about its hinge line (so that the hinge moments include the inertial forces).
AeroControlVector: A vector of values of the aerodynamic extra points (the control surfaces, rigid body motions and general controllers of a trim), which the user defined forces of an AeroDownwash, AeroForceVector or AeroPressureVector card are evaluated at.
AeroController: A general controller of a trim, an aerodynamic extra point whose forces come from the AeroDownwash, AeroForceVector and AeroPressureVector cards that name it.
AeroDivergence: The Mach numbers of a static aeroelastic divergence analysis.
AeroDownwash: The normal wash (downwash) loading that goes with one control vector of the aerodynamic configuration.
AeroFactorList: A list of real numbers that an aerodynamic card names by its set ID.
AeroFiniteBeamSpline7: A finite beam spline that maps the motion of structural grid points to the boxes (or aerodynamic grid points) of an AeroBoxList through a beam it builds, in all six degrees of freedom or in the three translations.
AeroFiniteSurfaceSpline6: A finite surface spline between two meshes in 6 or 3 degrees of freedom.
AeroFlutter: Selects the flutter solution method and the factor tables that define the flight conditions.
AeroFlutterFactors: A list of the density ratios, Mach numbers, reduced frequencies or velocities of a flutter analysis, that an AeroFlutter card names by its set ID.
AeroForceVector: A vector of forces, absolute or per unit dynamic pressure, that goes with one control vector of the aerodynamic configuration and is used by the static aeroelastic trim.
AeroGust: A stationary vertical gust for the aeroelastic response analyses.
AeroLabelList: Defines a named list of short labels for reference by other aeroelastic records.
AeroLiftingPanel1: Defines a lifting-surface panel by its leading-edge endpoints and the chord at each end.
AeroLiftingPanelProp1: The property of the AeroLiftingPanel1 panels that name it, which lists the aerodynamic bodies (AeroBody2 cards) that interact with them in the Doublet-Lattice method.
AeroMachBoxPanel3: The edges of an aerodynamic surface for the Mach box method.
AeroMachBoxProp3: The property of the AeroMachBoxPanel3 Mach box surfaces that name it, with the number of boxes in the flow direction and the cranks and control surfaces of the planform.
AeroMachFreqPairs2: A list of Mach number and reduced frequency pairs for the aerodynamic matrices.
AeroMachFreqTable1: A table of Mach numbers and reduced frequencies at which the aerodynamic matrices are computed.
AeroNode: A grid point of an aerodynamic mesh that the AeroQuad4 and AeroTria3 cards connect.
AeroNodeScale: The reference lengths that scale the coordinates of the aerodynamic grid points (AeroNode) which name it.
AeroPistonPanel5: An aerodynamic macro element for piston theory, a panel cut into strips that span the whole chord.
AeroPistonProp5: The properties of the strips of an AeroPistonPanel5 panel (piston theory): the angle of attack, the chordwise coordinates and the thickness ratios that the AeroFactorList cards list, and the control surface chord of every strip.
AeroPressureVector: A vector of pressure per unit dynamic pressure that goes with one control vector of the aerodynamic configuration.
AeroPrismNodeSet2: Selects structural grid points inside a prism over an aerodynamic panel for use by a spline.
AeroQuad4: A quadrilateral element of an aerodynamic mesh, given by four aerodynamic grid points (AeroNode).
AeroRigidSpline: A rigid body spline that moves the boxes (or the aerodynamic grid points) of an AeroBoxList like a rigid body whose motion is given by six structural degrees of freedom, whatever the aerodynamic geometry is.
AeroRigidTrimVariable: A rigid body motion that is a variable of a static aeroelastic trim (the angle of attack, a rate, an acceleration of the aircraft).
AeroSplineCurveBlend: A curve based blend of two splines.
AeroSplineEquation3: A constraint equation that sets one component of motion of one aerodynamic box from the displacements of structural degrees of freedom, the way a control surface is tied to its actuator.
AeroSplineRelaxation: The relaxation of a spline on its neighbour.
AeroSplineStripBlend: A strip based blend of two splines, which the other splines name as their own (the blend has a spline ID of its own and may be blended again).
AeroStaticParams: The basic parameters of a static aeroelastic analysis (trim, divergence, stability derivatives).
AeroStripPanel4: An aerodynamic macro element for strip theory, a panel cut into strips that span the whole chord.
AeroStripProp4: The properties of the strips of an AeroStripPanel4 panel (strip theory): the lift curve slope and lag function selections, and the control surface of every strip.
AeroSurfaceSpline1: A surface spline that carries the displacements of a set of structural grid points to a regular array of aerodynamic boxes, and the aerodynamic forces back to the grid points.
AeroSurfaceSpline4: A surface spline like AeroSurfaceSpline1, for any aerodynamic geometry: the points it moves are listed in an AeroBoxList instead of being a run of box numbers.
AeroTria3: A triangular element of an aerodynamic mesh, given by three aerodynamic grid points (AeroNode).
AeroTrim: The flight condition of a static aeroelastic trim and the trim variables that are fixed in it.
AeroTrim2: Defines a flight condition and the values of its trim variables for static aeroelastic analysis.
AeroTrimLink: A linear relation that fixes one trim variable (the dependent one) as a combination of others, so that the trim does not solve for it.
AeroUnsteadyParams: The basic aerodynamic parameters of the unsteady analyses (flutter, frequency and transient response to a gust).
AeroUserSpline: A spline that a program supplied by the user evaluates, instead of one of the methods of the format.
AnalysisDofSet: Degrees of freedom of the analysis set (a-set).
AnalysisDofSet1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points in the analysis set (a-set).
AnisoMat2D: An anisotropic material for two-dimensional elements.
AnisoMat2DFreq: The frequency dependence of the properties of an AnisoMat2D (a shell element anisotropic material).
AnisoMat2DTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of an AnisoMat2D.
AnisoMat3D: An anisotropic material for solid elements.
AnisoMat3DFreq: The frequency dependence of the properties of an AnisoMat3D (a solid element anisotropic material).
AnisoMat3DTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of an AnisoMat3D.
ArcLengthParams: The arc-length method of a nonlinear static analysis.
AssociativeNode: Associates a grid point with the assembly step that combines model parts.
AutoConstrExclusion: Excludes specified point components from automatic singularity constraints.
AutoConstrExclusionList: Excludes the same specified components at a list of points from automatic singularity constraints.
AxialDeformationLoad: Enforced axial deformations of one-dimensional elements, for static analysis.
AxisymConeControl: Identifies the model as an axisymmetric conical shell system using rings, shell elements and ring loads.
AxisymConePoint: Defines a point on a conical shell ring for concentrated loads and displacement recovery.
AxisymConePressureLoad: The static pressure on a conical shell element, the one between two rings over an azimuthal sector.
AxisymConeRing: A ring of a conical shell model (an axisymmetric structure described by harmonics).
AxisymConeSector: A sector of a conical shell.
AxisymConeSupport: The fictitious supports of a conical shell free body, the determinate reactions of the analysis.
AxisymConeTemperatureLoad: The temperature of a ring of a conical shell model at an azimuth angle.
AxisymFluid2: Defines an axisymmetric fluid element generated by revolving a two-corner cross-section.
AxisymFluid3: Defines an axisymmetric fluid element generated by revolving a triangular cross-section.
AxisymFluid4: Defines an axisymmetric fluid element generated by revolving a quadrilateral cross-section.
AxisymFluidBoundaryList: The fluid points (AxisymFluidRing) of the boundary between an axisymmetric fluid and a structure.
AxisymFluidControl: The basic parameters and the existence of an axisymmetric fluid analysis, with the harmonics of the solution.
AxisymFluidFreePoint: A point on the free surface of an axisymmetric fluid at which the surface displacements are recovered.
AxisymFluidFreeSurface: The fluid points (AxisymFluidRing) of a free surface boundary of an axisymmetric fluid model.
AxisymFluidPressurePoint: A point of an axisymmetric fluid at which the pressure is recovered, and that may also measure pressure for a control device.
AxisymFluidRing: A circle of an axisymmetric fluid model.
AxisymFluidRingNode: A grid point on a fluid ring (AxisymFluidRing) of an axisymmetric model.
AxisymFluidSymmetry: The symmetry of the structural boundary of an axisymmetric fluid model.
AxisymHarmonicProp: The properties of the linear axisymmetric harmonic elements AxisymQuad and AxisymTria.
AxisymOmittedDofSet: Degrees of freedom of a conical shell model that are excluded (the o-set) from the analysis set (the a-set).
AxisymOrthoMat: A linear orthotropic material for the axisymmetric elements (AxisymTria6) and the PlaneCompProp and PlanePropNonlinearExt entries; x, theta (the azimuthal direction) and z are the material axes.
AxisymOrthoMatStressDependent: Extends an axisymmetric orthotropic material with nonlinear elastic data.
AxisymOrthoMatTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of an AxisymOrthoMat.
AxisymQuad: An axisymmetric quadrilateral element with four corners, up to four edge points and an optional centre point.
AxisymQuad4: A four-node axisymmetric quadrilateral ring element.
AxisymQuad8: An axisymmetric quadrilateral ring element with four corners and up to four edge points.
AxisymRingForceLoad: A static concentrated force on a ring of a conical shell model (it needs an AxisymConeControl card).
AxisymRingMomentLoad: A static concentrated moment on a ring of a conical shell model.
AxisymShellProp: The property of the axisymmetric line element ShellAxisym.
AxisymTractionLoad: A surface traction on the side of an axisymmetric element (ShellAxisym, AxisymQuad, AxisymTria, AxisymTria6).
AxisymTria: An axisymmetric triangular element with three corners and up to three edge points.
AxisymTria6: An axisymmetric triangular cross-section ring element with up to six grid points.
Bar2Defaults: Supplies default property, orientation and offset conventions for Bar2 elements whose corresponding fields are blank.
Bar2Stations: Extra stations along a bar element where stresses and forces are recovered.
BarArbitrarySectionProp: The arbitrary cross-section of a Bar2, described by the points of a set of GeomPoint cards.
BarProp: The property of a simple beam element (Bar2).
BarPropNonlinear: The nonlinear extension of the BarProp or BarShapeProp with the same property ID.
BarShapeProp: A simple beam property given by the dimensions of its cross-section.
Beam2: A two-node beam carrying axial force, bending moments, torsion and transverse shear. Its property describes the cross-section and its orientation defines the local bending axes.
Beam2Defaults: Supplies default property, orientation and offset conventions for Beam2 elements whose corresponding fields are blank.
Beam3: A three-node beam element (ends A and B and a middle point C).
Beam3DistributedLoad: A distributed load on a Beam3 element, over the whole length of the beam axis, along the line of the shear center.
Beam3TemperatureLoad: The temperature field of the three-node beam element Beam3.
BeamArbitrarySectionProp: The arbitrary cross-section of a Beam2 (or, with a Core or a Layer, of a Beam3), described by the points of a set of GeomPoint cards.
BeamDistributedLoad: A concentrated or distributed load on a Bar2, Beam2 or CurvedBeam2 element.
BeamLumpedAreaProp: The alternate form of a BeamProp for a uniform beam, with the lumped areas of its cross-section.
BeamProp: The property of a beam element (Beam2) that may taper.
BeamProp3: The property of a three-node beam element (Beam3).
BeamPropNonlinear: The nonlinear extension of the BeamProp or BeamShapeProp with the same property ID.
BeamShapeProp: A beam property given by the dimensions of its cross-section, possibly different at several stations along the element.
BeltProp: The property of a belt element, a Rod2 that names the card in its property ID field.
BoltConnection: Represents a bolt cut by tying pairs of grid points on opposite sides to a common control node. A force or prescribed motion at this node applies pretension.
BoltPretension: Defines a bolt pretension section through a layer of elements. An axial force or displacement at the control node loads the section.
BrakeMotion: The motion direction of a body of a brake system, which a BrakeSystem names (MT1_ID, MT2_ID).
BrakeProp: The property of a brake system for the brake squeal analysis, named by a BrakeSystem.
BrakeSqueal: The data of a brake squeal analysis of one wheel, or of another rotating object in contact with friction between sets of bodies (unsymmetric friction stiffness matrices).
BrakeSystem: The data of a brake system for brake squeal calculations with one wheel or several, on one axis or several.
BucklingEigenMethod: Specifies the extraction data for a buckling eigenvalue problem.
BulkViscosityMat: The bulk viscosity of a material.
BushProp: The property of a generalized spring-and-damper (Bushing).
BushProp1D: The property of a rod type spring-and-damper (Bushing1D).
BushProp2D: The linear and nonlinear properties of the two-dimensional bush Bushing2D.
BushProp2DFreq: The frequency dependent stiffness, damping and mass of the BushProp2D with the same ID, each term given by the TableDynamic1 that holds its variation against frequency.
BushPropFreq: The frequency dependent or nonlinear properties of the BushProp with the same ID.
Bushing1D: A rod-type spring and damper between two grid points.
Bushing2D: Models an in-plane connection between the inner and outer grid points of a bearing or bushing.
CampbellDiagram: The parameters of the generation of a Campbell diagram and of the tracking of the modes along it.
CohesiveAxisymQuad: A linear or quadratic axisymmetric cohesive interface element with four to eight nodes, used to simulate the onset and growth of a delamination between two axisymmetric bodies.
CohesiveFriction: A cohesive friction, which lets friction and sticking act at the coupling surface while the Euler material pulls on it (tension).
CohesiveHexa: A linear or quadratic three-dimensional cohesive interface element with eight to twenty nodes, used to simulate the onset and growth of a delamination between two bodies.
CohesiveMat: The material of the interface cohesive zone elements that simulate the onset and the growth of a delamination.
CohesivePenta: A linear or quadratic three-dimensional cohesive interface element with six to fifteen nodes (a wedge), used to simulate the onset and growth of a delamination between two bodies.
CohesiveProp: The property of the interface cohesive zone elements (CohesiveQuad, CohesiveHexa, CohesivePenta and CohesiveAxisymQuad), which simulate the onset and growth of a delamination.
CohesiveQuad: A linear or quadratic planar cohesive interface element with four to eight nodes, used to simulate the onset and growth of a delamination between two bodies in plane strain or plane stress.
ColdGasInflator: A cold gas inflator, a tank of compressed gas that empties into a gas bag (GasBag) or an Euler coupling surface (EulerLagrangeCoupling) through the InflatorInlet that names the card.
CompProp: The property of a layered composite shell.
CompPropExplicit: The additional data of a CompProp, with the options of the explicit shell elements.
CompPropFreqDamping: The frequency dependent structural damping of the CompProp or CompPropGlobal with the same property ID.
CompPropGlobal: The property of a layered composite shell whose plies have global ply IDs.
CompPropIntegration: The through-the-thickness integration procedure of the composite shells whose CompProp or CompPropGlobal is in the list.
CompSolidProp: The property of a layered composite solid, which a solid element names.
CompSolidPropNonlinear: The property of a layered solid composite, which a SolidHexa names.
ComplexEigenMethod: The data of a complex eigenvalue extraction.
ComplexEigenPoles: Supplies one or two poles for the determinant-based complex eigenvalue method.
ConicalShellProp: The property of the conical shell elements (ShellConical2).
ConnectorSearchControl: Values of the parameters of the connector search that apply to a group of connector elements (Fastener, Seam, Weld) and override the ones of the ConnectorSearchParams card for them.
ConnectorSearchParams: Sets named search controls for finding the surfaces joined by Fastener, Weld and Seam elements.
ConstantSpallation: The constant spallation model, in which the minimum pressure is constant.
ContactAutoParams: Specifies name–value settings for automatic contact generation.
ContactBeamCap: Whether a cap is added to a beam and how many segments model a rod or tube section, for the segment-to-segment beam contact.
ContactBeamRadius: The equivalent radius of beams for the node-to-segment beam-to-beam contact: the radius of the beam elements or bodies it lists, or the default radius of all beam elements.
ContactBeamSectionFlags: The branches and segments of a beam section that take part in the segment-to-segment beam contact.
ContactBezierSurface: A rigid contact body made of a Bezier surface.
ContactBody: A flexible or rigid contact body in 2D or 3D.
ContactBody1: A flexible or rigid contact body, the new form of ContactBody.
ContactBodyChange: Changes the definition of the deformable contact bodies in a load case.
ContactBodyMove: The movement of bodies in contact in a load case: the rigid bodies are moved until they touch the deformable ones, or the contact of some bodies is released.
ContactBodyParams: The parameters of a contact body: friction, spline smoothing of the surface, check of the contact conditions, heat transfer coefficients, as (name, value) pairs.
ContactBoxRegion: Selects elements inside a three-dimensional box as a region of a contact body.
ContactControlParams: The control parameters of the contact algorithm of the contact set that has the same number, as (name, value) pairs.
ContactElemSurface: Defines the elements forming a contact surface for a contact body.
ContactEllipsoidList: Groups the named contact ellipsoids of an occupant model.
ContactFaceRegion: A contact region made of element faces, named by ContactPair.
ContactMaterialRegion: Selects elements by material to form a three-dimensional contact region.
ContactNodeRegion: A contact region made of a list of grid points.
ContactNurbsCurve: A 2D rigid contact body made of a NURBS curve.
ContactNurbsSurface: A rigid contact body made of a NURBS surface.
ContactPair: A contact pair: the bodies that touch (secondary, the "touching" bodies) and the bodies they touch (primary), with the parameter sets of the pair.
ContactPairGeomParams: Sets geometric controls for a contact pair, including search order, interference fit, glue and the initial gap.
ContactPairPhysicalParams: Sets the physical interaction between a pair of contact bodies, including friction, thermal contact and glue failure.
ContactParams: Sets named controls for contact detection and response, including separation, friction and geometric tolerance.
ContactPatchSurface: A rigid contact body made of quadrilateral patches.
ContactPropertyRegion: Selects elements by property to form a three-dimensional contact region.
ContactRigidMotion: The motion of a rigid contact body.
ContactRigidSurfaceList: Collects rigid surface descriptions into a single region that a contact body can reference.
ContactSegment: A segment of a contact surfacegiven by the grid points of an element face.
ContactSet: A contact set of the older contact definition.
ContactSetUnion: Combines several contact sets into one selectable set.
ContactSlideline: Defines the primary and secondary lines for sliding contact, together with the stiffness, friction and penetration settings.
ContactSurfaceParams: Sets surface interaction options such as normal orientation, stiffness, tying, offsets and activation times.
ContactTable: Defines which contact bodies interact in a load case and the associated contact or glue conditions.
ContactTable1: The contact table of a load case, a list of ContactPair contact pairs.
ContactTrimCurve: The geometry of a trimming curve of a NURBS surface of a rigid contact body.
ContactUnglueNodes: The grid points of a contact body that are taken out of glued contact and use standard contact instead (for a crack, the points along it).
ContactUserService: Associates a contact body with a user routine and supplies the integer, real and text arguments it receives.
CosimulationArea: The coupled area through which the solver exchanges data with a co-simulation partner.
CosimulationInputs: The physical quantities of input that the solver receives from the co-simulation partner.
CosimulationOutputs: The physical quantities of output that the solver provides to the co-simulation partner.
CosimulationSelection: The co-simulation services an analysis uses, listed by the number of their CosimulationService.
CosimulationService: A co-simulation service, with the coupled areas and the physical quantities it exchanges.
CouplingCohesiveFriction: A cohesive friction model on one part of the coupling surface of an EulerLagrangeCoupling.
CouplingFailedSegmentFlow: The state of the surroundings that flows through a segment of a coupling surface after the segment fails (the structure that carries it breaks).
CouplingHoleToCoupling: A hole in a coupling surface through which gas flows to another coupling surface.
CouplingHoleToGasBag: A hole in an EulerLagrangeCoupling or GasBag (sub)surface that is connected to another GasBag, to model the flow between two air bags (two GasBags, a GasBag and an Eulerian air bag, or two Eulerian air bags).
CouplingInteraction: An interaction between two coupling surfaces that becomes active when the structure that carries them fails.
CouplingOptions: Special options of one part of the coupling surface of an EulerLagrangeCoupling: the factor that scales the Eulerian pressure acting on it and a pressure load from the covered side.
CrackClosureCrack: A crack for the virtual crack closure technique, with the options of its growth, the resistance of the material and the grid points of the crack front.
CrackTip2D: Represents a two-dimensional crack-tip element associated with UserDefined8Attributes.
CrackTip3D: Represents a three-dimensional crack-tip element associated with UserDefined9Attributes.
CrackTipProp2D: The property of a CrackTip2D crack tip element.
CrackTipProp3D: The property of a CrackTip3D crack tip element.
CreepMat: The creep characteristics of an IsoMat, AnisoMat2D or AnisoMat3D, from an empirical creep law or from tables.
CrossSpectrumPair: Pairs two response quantities for cross-power spectral density or cross-correlation recovery.
CurvedBeam2: A curved beam, curved pipe or elbow element between two grid points.
CurvedBeamProp: The property of a curved beam, curved pipe or elbow (CurvedBeam2).
CyclicAxisNodes: The grid points that lie on the axis of symmetry of a cyclic symmetry model.
CyclicAzimuthTableLoad: Loads of an axisymmetric cyclic model as a function of the azimuth angle, from a table of scale factors and a load set (two pairs at most).
CyclicBoundaryJoin: The boundary points of one side of a segment in a cyclic symmetry problem.
CyclicHarmonicLoad: The harmonic coefficients of a static or dynamic load of a cyclic symmetry model.
CyclicSegmentLoad: A physical load on a segment of a cyclic symmetry model, from one or two load sets.
CyclicSupport: The fictitious supports of a cyclic symmetry model.
CyclicSymmetry: The parameters of a cyclic symmetry analysis.
CylinderShape: Defines a cylindrical region used to select Eulerian elements for initial conditions or body forces.
CylindricalFrame1: One cylindrical coordinate system defined by three grid points.
CylindricalFrame2: A cylindrical coordinate system defined by three points.
DamperDofInline: A scalar damper that holds its own damping (no property).
DamperDofInlineExplicit: The scalar damper that holds its own damping (no property), with the coordinate system its direction is given in.
DamperDofProperty: A scalar damper that refers to a DamperProp property.
DamperDofPropertyExplicit: The scalar damper that names a property, with the coordinate system its direction is given in.
DamperProp: Supplies the viscous damping coefficient for scalar dampers that reference this property.
DamperPropFreq: The frequency dependent property of the DamperProp with the same ID.
DamperScalarInline: A scalar damper between two scalar points, with its own damping (no property).
DamperScalarProperty: A scalar damper between two scalar points, with a DamperProp property.
DeactivatedElems: The elements that do not take part in the analysis, or in one physics pass of a coupled analysis.
DefaultTemperatureLoad: Assigns a default temperature to nodes in a load set. A NodeTemperatureLoad in the same set overrides it at its node.
DeflagrationStateEquation: Stores a material equation-of-state definition for a reacting gas.
DesignBeadRegion: A design region of a topography (bead or stamp) optimisation: the nodes of the elements of one property, which the beads of the given size move.
DesignBoundaryShape: A boundary shape vector, as a combination of the vectors that the load sequences of an auxiliary model give.
DesignConstants: Named real constants for the equations of the design relations and responses.
DesignConstr: The bounds of one response, in a set of design constraints.
DesignConstrScreen: The screening of the constraints of one response type, to the most critical ones.
DesignConstrUnion: The design constraints of a subcase as the union of several DesignConstr sets.
DesignControlSurface: The setting of a control surface in a trim case as a design variable times a coefficient.
DesignDiscreteValues: Defines a list of admissible values for discrete design variables, topometry or rotor-speed selections.
DesignElemRelation1: A field of an element as a linear function of design variables.
DesignElemRelation2: A field of an element as the value of a DesignEquation equation of design variables and constants.
DesignFieldConstants: Constants that are the value of a field of a property, a material or a connection of the analysis model (taken before the design variables change it).
DesignLoadRelation1: A value of a load as a linear function of design variables.
DesignMatRelation1: A field of a material as a linear function of design variables.
DesignMatRelation2: A field of a material as the value of a DesignEquation equation of design variables and constants.
DesignNodeMove: How a design variable moves a grid point.
DesignOptimParams: Overrides named optimization controls in a design model.
DesignPropRelation1: A field of a property as a linear function of design variables.
DesignPropRelation2: A field of a property as the value of a DesignEquation equation of design variables and constants.
DesignResp1: Defines a structural response, such as weight, displacement, stress or frequency, for an optimization objective or constraint.
DesignResp2: Combines design variables, constants and other responses through a built-in function or a DesignEquation.
DesignResp3: A response computed by a routine of the user, from design variables, constants and other responses.
DesignShapeBasis: Defines a shape basis vector as a linear combination of displacement-matrix columns from a previous analysis.
DesignTopologyRegion: A region of a topology optimisation, the elements of one property whose density the optimisation designs.
DesignTopometryRegion: A design region of a topometry optimisation, in which the thickness or another property value of every element of one property is a design variable of its own.
DesignVar: Defines a design variable by its label, starting value and bounds. Design relations use its ID to vary model properties.
DesignVarLink: A design variable that is a linear function of other design variables.
DirectMatrix: Either the header of a matrix (the second field is the integer 0) or one column of it.
DirectMatrixAeroJ: Either the header of a matrix at the js-set of the aerodynamic mesh (the second field is the integer 0) or one column of it.
DirectMatrixAeroJInterference: Either the header of a matrix at the js-set of the aerodynamic mesh of the interference body of a AeroBody2 (the second field is the integer 0) or one column of it.
DirectMatrixAeroK: Either the header of a matrix at the ks-set of the aerodynamic mesh (the second field is the integer 0) or one column of it.
DirectMatrixAxisym: The matrix input of an axisymmetric analysis (a model with an AxisymFluidControl entry), either the header of a matrix (the second field is the integer 0) or one column of it.
DirectMatrixNodal: Either the header of a matrix (the second field is the integer 0) or one column of it.
DirectTable: Supplies a record of user data to a named table, preserving the order of its fields.
DofSetRenames: New names for the degree-of-freedom sets.
DynamicLoadCombination: A dynamic load made of other dynamic load sets, combined linearly.
DynamicLoadDelay: Time delays of a dynamic load on one or two degrees of freedom.
DynamicLoadPhase: Phase leads of a dynamic load on one or two degrees of freedom.
DynamicLoadScale: Scale (area) factors of a load on one or two degrees of freedom.
EchoOffMarker: Marks the point of the Bulk Data from which the printed echo of the input file is deactivated.
EchoOnMarker: Marks the point of the Bulk Data from which the printed echo of the input file is activated.
ElasticShearModel: An elastic shear model with a constant shear modulus.
ElastoPlasticMat: The elasto-plastic properties of a material (it extends an IsoMat, AnisoMat2D, OrthoMat3DNonlinear, OrthoMat2D or AnisoMat3D).
ElastoPlasticMatTemperature: The temperature dependence of the properties of an ElastoPlasticMat.
ElemGeneration: Defines how elements are generated from a field of grid points.
EnforcedMotionConstr: The value of an enforced motion (displacement, velocity or acceleration) of one or two grid points.
EulerBarrier: Faces of an Euler mesh that material cannot cross.
EulerBodyForce: A body force (an acceleration per unit mass) on the Eulerian elements, in the direction of a vector, scaled by a number, by a table of time, or by both.
EulerBodyForceSet: The body force of the Eulerian regions of a set.
EulerCyclicFlowBoundary: A cyclic (periodic) flow boundary of an Euler mesh.
EulerDefaultFlowBoundary: The default flow boundary of an Euler mesh, which the free faces that no EulerFlowBoundary, EulerTimeFlowBoundary or other boundary names take.
EulerFlowBoundary: A flow boundary of an Euler mesh with the properties of the material at the boundary.
EulerForceRegion: One Eulerian region (a shape and a material) with the time dependent acceleration that acts in it.
EulerHydrostaticPreset: Supplies the initial hydrostatic density distribution for an Eulerian fluid in a coupling region.
EulerInitialRegions: The initial conditions of the Eulerian regions.
EulerLagrangeCoupling: A general coupling surface, the interface between an Eulerian domain (finite volume) and a Lagrangian one (finite elements).
EulerMat: A general constitutive model for an Eulerian material: an equation of state, a shear model, a yield model, a failure model and a spall model.
EulerMeshBias: Specifies how cell size varies along one direction of a generated Eulerian mesh.
EulerMeshGenerator: The generator of an Eulerian mesh, either a box of elements or a mesh that adapts around a coupling surface.
EulerProp: The property of the Eulerian elements (SolidHexa and the elements an EulerMeshGenerator generates) that name its property ID.
EulerRegionProp: The property of Eulerian elements whose initial conditions are given in geometric regions (an EulerInitialRegions) instead of one material, as an EulerProp does.
EulerTimeFlowBoundary: A flow boundary of an Euler mesh whose inflow velocity, pressure and material properties may depend on time.
EulerUserFlowBoundary: A flow boundary of an Euler mesh that a user subroutine computes.
ExplicitParam: A named parameter of the explicit solver.
ExplicitTextEnd: Closes the opaque group opened by ExplicitTextStart.
ExplicitTextStart: Opens an opaque group of records for an external explicit solver.
ExtraPoint: Introduces an additional scalar degree of freedom for a dynamic model.
FabricMat: A bi-directional woven fabric material for shell elements, a fabric with an optional coating.
FacePressureLoad: A pressure on a face of a shell or solid element, or on a range of shell elements.
FailureMat: The failure model of the linear elastic material with the same ID.
FailureMatTemperature: The variation (with the temperature) of the failure properties of the FailureMat with the same ID.
Fastener: A fastener between two surface patches.
FastenerProp: The property of a fastener element (Fastener).
FastenerPropFreq: The frequency dependent and nonlinear properties of the FastenerProp with the same ID.
FatigueDefinition: The elements of a fatigue analysis and the fatigue properties each has, and how much of the result is kept (the top percentage of the entities, the number of hot spots).
FatigueEvent: Groups fatigue loading histories that act at the same time in a fatigue assessment.
FatigueLoad: Describes a load history or spectrum contributing to a fatigue event.
FatigueMat: The fatigue properties of an isotropic metal.
FatigueParams: The parameters of a fatigue analysis (type, combination of the stresses, mean stress correction, location of the results, and the lines for rainflow counting, certainty of survival, factor of safety, spot welds, seam welds, multiaxial assessment, nodal averaging, and vibration fatigue).
FatigueProp: Assigns fatigue properties to elements selected by a FatigueDefinition.
FatigueSequence: The sequence of loading events of a fatigue analysis (pseudo-static, modal, modal transient or random vibration), each with the number of times it is repeated, and possibly other sequences.
FixedBoundaryDofSet: Degrees of freedom of the fixed analysis set (b-set).
FixedBoundaryDofSet1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points in the fixed analysis set (b-set).
FixedBoundaryDofs: Degrees of freedom of the fixed boundary set (b-set) for the generalized dynamic reduction and the component mode synthesis.
FixedBoundaryDofs1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points in the fixed boundary set (b-set).
FluidFilledContainer: The pressure inside a closed volume that holds a fluid and a gas, for containers where the motion of the fluid does not matter (loading a bottle from the top, hot filling).
FluidMassElemList: A list of ShellQuad4 and ShellTria3 elements for the virtual fluid mass of a FluidVirtualMass.
FluidMat: The material of a fluid element in a coupled fluid-structure analysis.
FluidMatFreq: The frequency dependence of the properties of a FluidMat (a fluid material).
FluidStructureControl: Specifies the analysis mode of a coupled fluid–structure service.
FluidStructurePanels: Panels of the structure for the panel participation of a coupled fluid-structure analysis.
FluidStructureSwitch: The switch that turns the fluid-structure interaction and the Euler solver on and off in time.
FluidVirtualMass: The properties of an incompressible fluid volume, for the virtual mass matrix.
ForcedConvection: Applies forced convection to a tube-type heat-transfer surface.
ForcedConvectionProp: The forced convection property of the surface elements a ForcedConvection names.
FreeBodyLoad: An equilibrated free-body applied load case.
FreeBodySupport: The reference degrees of freedom of a free body (the r-set), which determine its rigid body motion.
FreeBodySupportSet: Identifies the reference degrees of freedom for a free body and groups them under a selectable set ID.
FreeBoundaryDofSet: Degrees of freedom of the free boundary set (c-set).
FreeBoundaryDofSet1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points in the free boundary set (c-set).
FreeBoundaryDofs: Degrees of freedom of the free boundary set (c-set) for the generalized dynamic reduction and the component mode synthesis.
FreeBoundaryDofs1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points in the free boundary set (c-set).
FreeConvection: The free convection boundary condition of a surface element.
FreeConvectionProp: The free convection property of the surface elements a FreeConvection names.
FreqBetweenModes3: Excitation frequencies between the modal frequencies of a range (modal frequency response).
FreqList: A set of excitation frequencies listed one by one.
FreqLogSteps2: Excitation frequencies at equal logarithmic steps.
FreqModeFractions5: Fractions of the modal frequencies of a range (modal frequency response).
FreqResponseLoad1: A frequency response excitation P(f) = A * (C(f) + i * D(f)) * exp(i * (phi - 2 * pi * f * tau)).
FreqResponseLoad2: A frequency response excitation P(f) = A * B(f) * exp(i * (phi(f) + phase - 2 * pi * f * tau)).
FreqSpreadAroundModes4: A spread of frequencies around each modal frequency of a range (modal frequency response).
FrfAssemblyLoadDelay: The time delay of a dynamic load on one degree of freedom of an FRF component, in an FRF based assembly (FBA).
FrfAssemblyLoadPhase: The phase lead of a dynamic load on one degree of freedom of an FRF component, in an FRF based assembly (FBA).
FrfAssemblyLoadScale: The scale factor of a dynamic load on one degree of freedom of an FRF component, in an FRF based assembly (FBA).
FrfComponent: A component whose frequency response functions were made by an earlier run and that an FRF based assembly (FBA) puts together with others.
FrfConnection: An explicit connection between a point of one FRF component and a point of another, in an FRF based assembly (FBA).
FrfExcitationDof: A degree of freedom where a unit load generates a frequency-response function. pointId identifies a node or scalar point. components is 1 to 6 for a node, 0 or blank for a scalar point. entryLabel is a required literal text value, preserved whole regardless of its length.
FrfExcitationDofList: Degrees of freedom where unit loads are applied to generate frequency response functions, for a list of points that share their components.
FrfFlexibleConnection: The stiffness, damping and structural damping of a flexible connection between a point of one FRF component and a point of another, in an FRF based assembly (FBA).
FrfReleasedDofs: Degrees of freedom of the connection grid points of FRF components that an FRF based assembly (FBA) does not connect.
FrfSinglePointConstr: Single-point constraints on connection points of FRF components in an FRF based assembly (FBA).
GammaLawStateEquation: The gamma law equation of state of a gas, p = (gamma - 1) rho e.
Gap2: A gap or friction element between two grid points.
GapProp: The property of a gap element (Gap2).
GasBag: Represents the uniform pressure within a closed volume enclosed by a coupling surface.
GasBagConvection: The heat transfer through convection from an air bag to its environment, through the surface of an EulerLagrangeCoupling or a GasBag.
GasBagHeatTransfer: A heat transfer definition of a part of the surface of a GasBag or an EulerLagrangeCoupling, which names the card that describes the transfer (a convection GasBagConvection, a radiation GasBagRadiation).
GasBagLeakage: A porosity definition of a part of the surface of a GasBag or an EulerLagrangeCoupling, which names the card that describes the flow (a hole, a permeable material, a flow boundary).
GasBagPermeableLink: A permeable area of an EulerLagrangeCoupling or GasBag surface that is connected to another GasBag.
GasBagRadiation: The heat transfer through radiation from an air bag to its environment, through the surface of an EulerLagrangeCoupling or a GasBag.
GasBagSwitch: The switch of an air bag from full gas dynamics (an EulerLagrangeCoupling, the Euler-Lagrange coupling) to the uniform pressure formulation (a GasBag).
GasBagVentHole: A hole in an EulerLagrangeCoupling or GasBag surface through which gas flows to the environment (a vent of an air bag).
GasketMat: Defines the nonlinear through-thickness compression response of a gasket and references the isotropic material supplying its membrane behavior.
GasketMatTemperature: The temperature dependence of the properties of a GasketMat.
GeneralFrame3: A general coordinate system whose three rotation angles are functions of the coordinates in the reference system.
GeneralMatrix: Defines an element by a stiffness or flexibility matrix over an ordered set of independent degrees of freedom. A separate matrix can relate a dependent set to them.
GeneralizedDofSet: Degrees of freedom of the generalized set (q-set).
GeneralizedDofSet1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points in the generalized set (q-set).
GeomBoundaryCurve: Defines a line-interface boundary from the ordered element edges along a geometric curve.
GeomPoint: A geometric point that is not a grid point (an edge point for SuperelementLocation, a profile point of a BeamArbitrarySectionProp).
GeomSinglePointConstr: Applies single-point constraints to the grid points associated with a geometric entity.
HeatAnisoMat: The anisotropic heat transfer material of a conduction element.
HeatAnisoMatTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of a HeatAnisoMat (anisotropic thermal conductivity).
HeatCapacity2: A damper (heat capacity, for heat transfer analysis) between two points, with a HeatCapacityProp5 property.
HeatCapacityProp5: The property of a HeatCapacity2 (a heat transfer damper: the mass that multiplies the heat capacity of a HeatIsoMat or HeatAnisoMat material).
HeatController: Identifies the control applied to a surface or volume heat source, convection condition or radiating boundary.
HeatFluxBoundaryLoad3: A uniform heat flux (or its multiplier) into a boundary surface.
HeatFluxNodalLoad2: The heat flux at each grid point of one surface element.
HeatFluxNodeSetLoad: A uniform heat flux into a set of grid points.
HeatFluxSurfaceLoad1: A uniform heat flux into surface elements.
HeatFluxVectorLoad: The thermal vector flux from a distant source into the faces of surface elements.
HeatIsoMat: The heat transfer material of a conduction element, and the fluid of a forced convection (ForcedConvection).
HeatIsoMatTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of a HeatIsoMat (thermal conductivity and related properties).
HeatShellInitialTemperature: The initial temperature of the grid points of heat shell elements (those of a ShellPropNonlinear heat transfer property) with a linear or quadratic temperature distribution across the thickness.
HeatShellNodalLoad: Concentrated static loads, a power input, on the grid points of heat shell elements (those of a ShellPropNonlinear heat transfer property) with a linear or quadratic temperature distribution through the thickness.
HeatSurfaceDefaults: The default values of the HeatSurfaceProperty, HeatSurfaceNodes and HeatSurfaceSide surface elements.
HeatSurfaceNodes: A boundary condition surface element defined by its grid points.
HeatSurfaceProp: The property of a HeatSurfaceProperty surface element.
HeatSurfaceProperty: A boundary condition surface element defined by grid points and a HeatSurfaceProp property.
HeatSurfaceSide: A boundary condition surface element that is one side of a heat conduction element.
HeatVolumeSourceLoad: Applies volumetric heat generation to a list of conduction elements.
HourglassSuppression: The hourglass suppression method and the damping coefficients of the elements of one property.
HybridDamping: The hybrid modal damping of a direct dynamic solution.
HybridDampingRotorOptions: Selects structural, material and Rayleigh damping contributions for hybrid modal damping of a rotor.
HybridInflator: A hybrid airbag inflator, which blows a mixture of gases into a GasBag or an Euler coupling surface (EulerLagrangeCoupling) through the InflatorInlet that names the card.
HybridInflatorFractions: Defines the time variation of constituent gas fractions for a HybridInflator.
HydrodynamicYield: The hydrodynamic yield model, a yield model whose yield stress is zero.
HydrostaticCavityLoad: A hydrostatic pressure load on the faces of shell and solid elements that are wetted by a fluid cavity.
HydrostaticLoad: Applies hydrostatic pressure to selected shell or solid faces using the specified fluid density and reference elevation.
HyperelasticMatTemperature: The temperature dependence of the coefficients of a HyperelasticMat.
HyperelasticPolynomialMat: A hyperelastic (rubber-like) material, the generalised Mooney-Rivlin strain energy function.
IdListSet1: Groups grid points or elements for selection by splines, interfaces and other model entries.
IgnitionGrowthStateEquation: Identifies a reactive equation-of-state record in the material data of an explicit model.
ImperfectionGeometry: The definition of a geometric imperfection, an ID that an ImperfectionCase names.
InflatorGas: Defines a thermally ideal gas used in a gas mixture or inflator model.
InflatorInlet: One inflator that blows into a gas bag (GasBag) or an Euler coupling surface (EulerLagrangeCoupling), on a part of their surface.
InitialConditionRegion: One Eulerian region (a shape and a material) with the set of initial values that its material starts with.
InitialConditionValues: The initial values of an Eulerian region, a list of variables and the value each starts with.
InitialElemValues: The initial values of element variables of the elements of an IdListSet1, at the start of the analysis.
InitialGasComposition: Specifies the initial mixture inside a GasBag or an EulerLagrangeCoupling surface.
InitialPlasticStrain: Initial equivalent plastic strain for a range of elements, integration points and layers.
InitialStress: An initial stress, for the elements, integration points and layers of a range.
InitialSurfaceVolume: An initialization surface, a closed volume (made of the segments of a ContactElemSurface) that a EulerInitialRegions region or an EulerForceRegion region uses to give initial conditions to the Eulerian elements inside or outside it.
InitialValuesUserRoutine: Initial values of element or grid point variables that a user written subroutine computes.
InitialVelocityField: An initial velocity field of grid points made of a translation and a rotation about a grid point.
IsoMat: An isotropic elastic material shared by element properties. Young’s modulus, shear modulus and Poisson’s ratio describe its elastic response.
IsoMatExplicitExt: The additional properties of an IsoMat for solid elements: the equation of state.
IsoMatFreq: The frequency dependence of the properties of an IsoMat (an isotropic material).
IsoMatStressDependent: The stress dependent properties of an IsoMat (nonlinear elasticity or plasticity).
IsoMatTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of an IsoMat.
JonesWilkinsLeeStateEquation: Stores a pressure–volume–energy equation-of-state definition for a material in an explicit model.
LanczosEigenMethod: Real eigenvalue extraction by the Lanczos method.
LineElemTemperatureLoad: The temperature field of one-dimensional elements (Bar2, Beam2, CurvedBeam2, Rod2, Tube2, Rod2InlineSection).
LineInterface: An interface ties at least two geometric boundary curves together.
LoadCaseIdLabel: Combines part loads selected by the load ID used to generate each part subcase.
LoadCaseNameLabel: Combines part loads selected by their case-control load names.
LoadCaseSubcaseLabel: Combines loads from different parts by selecting a subcase in each part.
LoadCombination: A static load made of other load sets, combined linearly.
MarkerBody: A marker element with two grid points, a line along which the Euler domain records its variables (time histories).
MarkerNode: A marker element with one grid point, a point at which the Euler domain records its variables (time histories).
MarkerProp: The property of the marker elements (MarkerBody and MarkerNode), which record the variables of the Euler domain at a point or along a line.
MassCaseCombination: The linear combination of mass cases that a subcase uses as its mass.
MassDofInline: A scalar mass element that holds its own mass value (no property).
MassDofProperty: A scalar mass element that refers to a MassProp property.
MassProp: One scalar mass property of a MassProp card.
MassScalarInline: A scalar mass element between two scalar points, with its own mass value (no property).
MassScalarProperty: A scalar mass element between two scalar points, with a MassProp property.
MaxPlasticStrainFailure: The maximum plastic strain failure model.
MetadataBooleanPairs: Stores boolean name/value pairs belonging to a MetadataGroup.
MetadataGroup: Entities of one kind added to a named group of the meta data written to the results files (it has no effect on the solution).
MetadataIntegerPairs: Stores integer name/value pairs belonging to a MetadataGroup.
MetadataRealPairs: Stores real name/value pairs belonging to a MetadataGroup.
MetadataTextPairs: Stores text name/value pairs belonging to a MetadataGroup.
MicromechanicsCompositeMat: The material data of an advanced composite modelled by a micromechanics tool.
MieGruneisenStateEquation: The Mie-Gruneisen equation of state, used for the pressure of solids under high strain rates (shock Hugoniot form).
ModeTracking: The mode tracking of a design optimization.
ModelParams: Parameters that affect the solution of the structural model.
ModuleBolt: Defines a pretensioned bolt spanning modules. A control point couples pairs of grid points on opposite sides of its cut.
ModuleBoundaryNodes: The grid points of a module that the automatic search of the boundary with another module, or with all the others, is limited to.
ModuleBrakeSystem: The data of a brake system for brake squeal calculations with one wheel or several, on one axis or several, in different modules.
ModuleBulkOptions: The type of a module and how the boundary between modules is searched.
ModuleBushing: A generalized spring-and-damper element whose end points may lie in different modules; the rules of the Bushing apply to it.
ModuleConnection: How the boundary points of the modules are connected at a location.
ModuleContactCandidates: The modules that are candidates for the automatic detection of contact across modules.
ModuleContactDetectParams: The parameters that detect contact pairs between bodies that lie in different modules when the contact is generated automatically, as (name, value) pairs.
ModuleContactPair: A contact pair whose touching and touched bodies lie in different modules: general contact, glued, step glued or permanently glued.
ModuleContactTable: Selects interactions involving bodies in different modules using their contact definitions.
ModuleDirectMatrix: The header of a matrix of direct input at points of several modules, or one column of it.
ModuleEntryExclusion: The Bulk Data entries of a primary module that a secondary (copied) module ignores.
ModuleExcludedNodes: The grid points of a module that are left out when the module is attached to another one (or to all the others): the counterpart of the ModuleBoundaryNodes, which limits the search to a list.
ModuleFastener: A fastener with a material orientation that connects two surface patches that lie in two modules (the multi-module counterpart of the Fastener).
ModuleFluidSet: Identifies the fluid points or elements in a module that participate in a FluidStructureInterface.
ModuleLabel: The label a module carries in the headings of the results output.
ModuleLocation: The position of a module in the main model, given by three points of the module and the three points of module 0 that they must be moved onto.
ModuleMirror1: A mirror image of a module in a plane given by three points of the main Bulk Data.
ModuleMirror2: A mirror image of a module in a plane given by two axes of a coordinate system.
ModuleMirrorPlane: A mirror image of a module (a primary or a secondary, copied one) in a plane given by three points of the main Bulk Data.
ModuleMoveSequence: The sequence of moves that repositions a module, given as the numbers of ModuleTranslation, ModuleRotation1, ModuleRotation2, ModuleMirror1 and ModuleMirror2 cards, applied in the order of the list.
ModuleMultiPointConstr: Defines a linear multipoint constraint using degrees of freedom in different modules.
ModuleResultFileParams: Records module-specific output settings that extend the model-level ResultFileParams definition.
ModuleRigidBodyStar: A rigid body whose six independent degrees of freedom are those of one grid point and whose dependent degrees of freedom are components of any number of other grid points, all of which may lie in different modules (the multi-module counterpart of the RigidBodyStar, whose rules apply).
ModuleRigidInterpolation: The motion of a reference grid point is the weighted average of the motion of other grid points, all of which may lie in different modules (the multi-module counterpart of the RigidInterpolation, whose rules apply).
ModuleRigidJoint: A rigid joint that connects two coinciding grid points that lie in two different modules (the multi-module counterpart of the RigidJoint, whose rules apply).
ModuleRigidRod: A pin-ended element that is rigid in translation and connects two grid points that lie in two modules (the multi-module counterpart of the RigidRod, whose rules apply).
ModuleRotation1: A rotation of a module about an axis given by two points of the main Bulk Data, optionally turning about a reference point.
ModuleRotation2: A rotation of a module about an axis of a coordinate system, optionally turning about a reference point.
ModuleSeam: A seam that connects two surface patches (shell elements) that lie in two modules (the multi-module counterpart of the Seam, whose rules apply).
ModuleStructureSet: Identifies the structural points or elements in a module that participate in a FluidStructureInterface.
ModuleTranslation: A translation of a module, given as a vector between two points of the main Bulk Data.
ModuleWeld: A weld or fastener that connects two surface patches, a point and a patch, or two points, between two modules (the multi-module counterpart of the Weld, whose rules apply).
MonitorChordNormalCoeffs: A monitor point of the stripwise normal force and pitching moment coefficients of the chordwise strips of AeroLiftingPanel1 panels (flutter and aeroelastic response).
MonitorGroup: A collection of monitor points that is available to the postprocessing.
MonitorNodeForceSum3: An integrated load monitor point that sums selected grid point forces.
MonitorSum: A new monitor result that is the weighted sum of existing monitor results (the SOLs that have monitor points: 101, 103, 108, 109, 111, 112, 144, 146, 200 and 400).
MonitorSumLocated: A new monitor result that is the weighted sum of existing monitor results, with a location.
MonitorSumTotal: Combines monitored forces and moments and transfers the moments to a common reference point.
MonteCarloParams: The parameters of a Monte-Carlo simulation by the non-parametric variability method.
MultiPointConstr: A multipoint constraint equation, the sum of Aj * u(Gj, Cj) = 0.
MultiPointConstrAxisym: A multipoint constraint equation of a conical shell, the sum of Aj * u(RIDj, HIDj, Cj) = 0.
MultiPointConstrUnion: A multipoint constraint set that is the union of other multipoint constraint sets.
MultiPointConstrValue: The load selectable right hand side Ym of one or two equations of non-homogeneous multipoint constraints (the MultiPointConstrWithValue cards).
MultiPointConstrWithValue: Defines a linear constraint on nodal degrees of freedom with a prescribed right-hand side.
NobleAbelStateEquation: The Noble-Abel equation of state of a gas, p = (gamma - 1) rho e / (1 - b rho), the ideal gas law corrected by the co-volume of the molecules.
Node: A grid point with a position, an input coordinate system and a coordinate system for its displacement components.
NodeDefaults: Supplies default position and displacement frames, permanent constraints and superelement membership for Node records with blank fields.
NodeSequence: The sequence in which grid and scalar points are ordered (manual resequencing).
NodeTemperatureLoad: The temperatures of some grid points.
NonStructMass: A set of non-structural mass, given per unit area or length on properties or elements.
NonStructMass1: Assigns one nonstructural mass value to a list of properties or elements.
NonStructMassLumped: A set of lumped non-structural mass, given as a total on properties or elements.
NonStructMassLumped1: The alternate form of NonStructMassLumped, one lumped non-structural mass shared by a list of properties or elements.
NonStructMassUnion: A set of non-structural mass that is the sum of other sets.
NonlinearAdaptiveStepping: Controls automatic load or time increments in a nonlinear analysis.
NonlinearBushForceTables: Defines the speed-dependent matrix of force tables referenced by a nonlinear bushing load.
NonlinearBushLoad3D: Applies a nonlinear three-dimensional force between coincident grid points as a function of relative displacement, velocity and rotor speed.
NonlinearHarmonicFreqContinuation: Specifies forcing frequencies used for continuation in a nonlinear harmonic analysis.
NonlinearHarmonicFreqList: The forcing frequencies of a nonlinear harmonic response, listed one by one.
NonlinearHarmonicFreqSteps: The forcing frequencies of a nonlinear harmonic response at equal steps.
NonlinearHarmonicParams: The parameters of a nonlinear harmonic response analysis.
NonlinearHarmonicSolverParams: Values for the parameters of the nonlinear frequency response analysis.
NonlinearMatOptions: The nonlinear material, composite and control options.
NonlinearNegativePowerLoad4: A nonlinear load that is a negative variable raised to a power.
NonlinearOutputItems: Selects additional quantities for nonlinear result output.
NonlinearPositivePowerLoad3: A nonlinear load that is a positive variable raised to a power.
NonlinearProductLoad2: A nonlinear load that is the product of two variables.
NonlinearRadialGap: Defines a circular gap between two coincident grid points for a nonlinear dynamic response.
NonlinearSqueezeFilmDamper: Defines the transient nonlinear forces from a radial squeeze-film damper between two grid points.
NonlinearStaticParams: The iteration strategy of a nonlinear static analysis.
NonlinearStepControl: The control parameters of the load or time stepping(mechanical, thermal and coupled analysis) and of the contact analysis.
NonlinearTableLoad1: A nonlinear load that is a tabular function of a displacement or a velocity.
NonlinearTimeSteps: The controls of a nonlinear transient analysis.
NonlinearUserOutput: Declares output quantities provided by a user routine for an explicit nonlinear analysis.
OccupantAccelField: An acceleration field, usually a crash pulse, that is applied to segments of the dummy of an external occupant model.
OccupantJoint: The interface to one joint of the dummy of an external occupant model.
OccupantSegment: Defines the position, orientation and identification of a segment in an occupant model.
OmittedDofSet: Degrees of freedom of the omitted set (o-set).
OmittedDofSet1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points in the omitted set (o-set).
OrthoMat2D: An orthotropic material for shell elements.
OrthoMat2DFailure: The failure properties of an orthotropic material for shell elements; the OrthoMat2D with the same ID holds the elastic constants.
OrthoMat2DFreq: The frequency dependence of the properties of an OrthoMat2D (a shell element orthotropic material).
OrthoMat2DStressDependent: Adds nonlinear elastic behavior to an OrthoMat2D material used in shells or plane stress.
OrthoMat2DTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of an OrthoMat2D.
OrthoMat3D: Defines orthotropic elastic properties for a solid material in its three material directions.
OrthoMat3DNonlinear: Defines a three-dimensional orthotropic material with optional plastic yielding for nonlinear solid elements.
OrthoMat3DNonlinearStressDependent: Adds nonlinear elastic behavior to an OrthoMat3DNonlinear solid material.
OrthoMat3DNonlinearTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of an OrthoMat3DNonlinear.
OrthoMat3DTemperature: The temperature dependent properties of an OrthoMat3D.
Parameter: A named parameter of the analysis.
PerforatedShellProp: Defines a perforated shell property for a porous elastic trim layer.
PlaneCompProp: The property of a plane strain or axisymmetric composite, which a PlaneStrainQuad, ShellQuad4, ShellQuad8 or AxisymQuad names.
PlaneProp: Supplies thickness and nonstructural mass for a plane stress or plane strain element.
PlanePropNonlinear: The property of a fully nonlinear plane strain, plane stress or axisymmetric element.
PlanePropNonlinearExt: The nonlinear extension of the PlanePropNonlinear with the same property ID, for the plane stress, plane strain and axisymmetric elements (ShellQuad4, PlaneStrainQuad, ShellQuad8, ShellTria3, ShellTria6, AxisymQuad, AxisymTria) that name it.
PlaneStrainQuad: A fully nonlinear plane strain quadrilateral element (PlanePropNonlinear or PlaneCompProp property) with four corners, up to four edge points and an optional centre point.
PlaneStrainQuad8: A plane strain quadrilateral with four corners and up to four edge points.
PlaneStrainTria6: A plane strain triangle with three corners and up to three edge points.
PlaneStressQuad8: A plane stress quadrilateral with four corners and up to four edge points.
PlaneStressTria6: A plane stress triangle with three corners and up to three edge points.
PlateTemperatureLoad: The temperature field of plate, membrane and composite elements, as an average temperature and a gradient through the thickness.
PlotLine2: A dummy line element that is only drawn on plots.
PlotQuad4: A dummy quadrilateral that is only drawn on plots.
PlotSurface: Describes a surface mesh used for display, including structural or cavity boundaries.
PlotTria3: A dummy triangle that is only drawn on plots.
PointForceLoad: A concentrated force at a grid point.
PointForceLoad1: A concentrated force at a grid point whose direction is the line from G1 to G2.
PointForceLoad2: A concentrated force at a grid point whose direction is the cross product of the vector from G1 to G2 with the vector from G3 to G4.
PointMassInertia: A concentrated mass at a grid point, with its own offset and inertia.
PointMassMatrix: A concentrated mass at a grid point, given as a full 6 x 6 symmetric mass matrix.
PointMomentLoad: A concentrated moment at a grid point.
PointMomentLoad1: A concentrated moment at a grid point whose axis is the line from G1 to G2.
PointMomentLoad2: A concentrated moment at a grid point whose axis is the cross product of the vector from G1 to G2 with the vector from G3 to G4.
PointsPressureLoad: A uniform pressure on the triangle or quadrilateral defined by three or four grid points.
PolynomialShearModel: An elastic shear model whose modulus is a cubic polynomial of the effective plastic shear strain gamma: G = G0 + G1 gamma + G2 gamma^2 + G3 gamma^3.
PolynomialStateEquation: The polynomial equation of state of a solid.
PoroElasticMat: An isotropic poroelastic material (the solid skeleton and the fluid of a porous medium), referenced by the SolidProp of a poroelastic solid.
PoroElasticMatFreq: The frequency dependent properties of an isotropic poroelastic material (it extends the IsoMat with the same ID, and a PoroElasticMat refers to it).
PorousFlowBoundary: The properties of a flow of material through a porous part of a coupling surface (a constant flow boundary): the velocity, pressure, density and energy of what flows, the material and the kind of boundary.
PorousHydrostaticBoundary: A porous flow boundary that prescribes a hydrostatic pressure profile on a part of a coupling surface.
PorousTimeFlowBoundary: A flow boundary through a porous part of a coupling surface whose velocity, pressure, density and energy vary with time.
PorousUserBoundary: A porosity model of an EulerLagrangeCoupling surface written by the user as a subroutine, served by a user defined service.
ProgressiveFailureMat: The progressive failure properties of an orthotropic material by the Cuntze-Bold material model (2D and 3D).
PropDistribution: A spatial distribution of one datum of a property.
PropMatDistribution: A spatial distribution of one material of a property.
PropertyListSet4: A list of property IDs of one type, which a FatigueDefinition (the fatigue definition) names.
RadiatedPowerPanelSet: Any number of panels, each a label and the TypedListSet3 of the elements or the properties that make it up.
RadiationBands: Planck's second radiation constant and the wavelength breakpoints of the radiation exchange problems, for the RadiationProp entries that give an emissivity for each wave band.
RadiationCavity: The characteristics of one radiation enclosure (cavity).
RadiationCavityList: The surface elements of a radiation enclosure.
RadiationCavitySet: The radiation cavities that take part in the enclosure radiation analysis.
RadiationExchangeMatrix: One column of the radiation exchange matrix of a cavity.
RadiationProp: Supplies radiative properties for the sides of heat-transfer surfaces.
RadiationPropTemperature: The tables that make the radiation properties of a RadiationProp depend on temperature.
RadiationToSpace: The radiation to space from surface element faces.
RandomSpectralDensity: A power spectral density factor of a random analysis.
RandomTimeLags: The time lags of the autocorrelation function of a random analysis.
RatePowerLawYield: The rate power law yield model.
RealEigenMethod: Real eigenvalue extraction, with the method named on the card.
RectFrame1: One rectangular coordinate system defined by three grid points.
RectFrame2: A rectangular coordinate system defined by three points.
RectFrame3: One moving rectangular coordinate system defined by three grid points.
ReferenceRotor: The reference rotor of the non-reference rotors of the residual structure, for a complex eigenvalue analysis.
RelativeEnforcedMotionConstr: The value of an enforced relative motion of one or two grid points, taken with respect to the position they had at the previous load step.
ResidualVectorDofs: Degrees of freedom where unit loads are applied to get the static solutions that the residual vector computation uses.
ResidualVectorDofs1: The degrees of freedom C of a list of points where unit loads are applied to get the static solutions that the residual vector computation uses.
ResultFileModules: Selects separate or appended results files for individual model modules.
ResultFileParams: Stores named results-file settings such as precision, compression and output selection.
ResultMetadata: Attaches user-supplied descriptive metadata to analysis results.
RigidAxisymConnection: A rigid connection between a point of an axisymmetric harmonic element (AxisymQuad or AxisymTria) and a point of the three-dimensional model on the axis of symmetry.
RigidBar: A rigid bar with six degrees of freedom at each end.
RigidBar1: Ties selected motion components of the second endpoint of a rigid bar to the first.
RigidBodyJoint: A joint between two rigid bodies.
RigidBodyMulti: A rigid body connected to any number of grid points, with its independent components given point by point.
RigidBodySearched: A RigidBodyStar that the solver builds itself.
RigidBodyStar: A rigid body whose independent degrees of freedom are the six of one grid point and whose dependent degrees of freedom are some components of any number of other grid points.
RigidEllipsoidExternal: The external definition of a rigid ellipsoid, whose properties and motion come from another program.
RigidInterpolation: The motion of a reference grid point is the weighted average of the motion of other grid points.
RigidInterpolationOverride: Sets a perturbation for coincident points of selected rigid interpolation elements.
RigidJoint: A rigid joint connecting two coinciding grid points.
RigidMat: A rigid material (a rigid body is the elements whose properties name it).
RigidMeshConnection: A rigid connection that ties two parts of Lagrangian meshes together (two surfaces, grid points to a surface, or the edge of shells to a shell surface).
RigidRod: A pin-ended element that is rigid in translation.
RigidShellSolidConnection: A clamped connection between a shell and a solid element (multipoint constraints).
RigidSpline: Multipoint constraints that interpolate the displacements of grid points along an elastic beam.
RigidTriaPlate1: Ties selected motion components of the second and third points of a rigid triangular plate to the first point.
RigidWall: Defines an infinite fixed plane serving as a contact boundary for a set of grid points.
Rod2: A two-node line element for axial and torsional response. The rod property connects the element to its material and cross-section.
Rod2InlineSection: A rod element with its own area and torsional constant, no property entry.
RodProp: Defines the material, cross-sectional area and torsional constants for rod elements.
RodPropNonlinear: The nonlinear extension of the RodProp with the same property ID.
RotationalForceLoad: A static load from an angular velocity and/or an angular acceleration about an axis.
RotorAxisym: The elements, the properties or the grid points that make an axisymmetric rotor.
RotorHybridDamping: Associates individual rotors with their hybrid modal damping definitions.
RotorInitialBend: The initial deformation of a rotor, made of kinks and offsets, which the rotor takes on before it is pulled onto its bearing and analysed.
RotorLineNodes: The grids that make the line model of a rotor.
RotorModel3D: The 3D model of a rotor, as the elements or the properties that make it and the grid points of its axis of rotation.
RotorRelativeSpin: The spin rate of a rotor relative to the others, for a complex eigenvalue, a frequency response or a static analysis, and the damping of the rotor.
RotorSuperelement: The rotor line model of a rotor that is placed in a superelement (the alternative to a RotorLineNodes when superelements are used).
RotorTransientSpin: The spin rate of a rotor in a transient analysis, and the damping of the rotor.
RotorUnbalanceLoad: A rotating unbalance load of a rotordynamic transient or frequency response analysis.
RotordynamicParams: The parameters of a rotordynamic analysis.
ScalarPoint: Defines scalar grid-free degrees of freedom by their point identifiers.
ScalarPointLoad: Concentrated static loads on scalar or grid points.
Seam: A seam that connects two surface patches (shell elements).
SeamProp: The property of a Seam seam connection.
ShapeBoundaryNodeSet: The grid points on the boundary of a shape optimisation, with the components for which the boundary motion is prescribed (they form the s-set).
ShearPanel4: A shear panel element with four corner grid points.
ShearPanelProp: The property of a shear panel (ShearPanel4).
ShearPanelPropNonlinear: The nonlinear extension of the ShearPanelProp with the same property ID.
ShellAxisym: An axisymmetric thick shell line element with two end points and, optionally, a third point between them on the curve of the element.
ShellConical2: An axisymmetric conical shell element between two rings, with a ConicalShellProp property.
ShellNormal: The surface normal vector at a grid point, for the ShellQuad4, ShellQuad4Drilling, ShellTria3 and ShellTria3Drilling shell elements.
ShellPressureLoad: A uniform pressure normal to a list of shell elements (ShellQuad4, ShearPanel4, ShellTria3).
ShellProp: Defines the membrane, bending and transverse-shear material associations and the reference thickness of a shell.
ShellPropNodal: The property of a shell with a thickness at each grid point, a formulation and the options of the explicit shell elements.
ShellPropNonlinear: The nonlinear extension of the ShellProp, CompProp or CompPropGlobal with the same property ID, for the shell elements (ShellQuad4, ShellQuad4Drilling, ShellQuad8, ShellTria3, ShellTria3Drilling, ShellTria6) that name it.
ShellQuad4Drilling: A four-node plate element with a drilling rotation.
ShellQuad8: A curved quadrilateral shell element with four corners and up to four edge points.
ShellTria3Drilling: A three-node plate element with a drilling rotation.
ShellTria6: A curved triangular shell element with three corners and up to three edge points.
SinglePointConstr: Single point constraints, with an enforced motion, on one or two grid points.
SinglePointConstrAxisym: A single point constraint or an enforced displacement of a conical shell coordinate.
SinglePointConstrList: Single point constraints on a list of grid points.
SinglePointConstrUnion: A constraint set that is the union of other constraint sets.
SlidelineFriction: The friction between two bodies of a slideline contact region.
SlidelineOutput: The secondary nodes at which a slideline contact analysis writes output.
SlidelineSegments: A curve of line segments of a slideline contact region, given by its grid points in topological order (one segment between every two consecutive points).
SlidelineWidth: The width (3-D slideline) or thickness (2-D) of each line segment of the SlidelineSegments of the same ID.
SnowMultiSurfaceYield: The multi-surface yield model of snow.
SolidHexa: A hexahedral solid with eight corner nodes and up to twelve additional edge nodes.
SolidPenta: A prismatic solid with six corner nodes and up to nine additional edge nodes.
SolidProp: The property of solid elements (SolidHexa, SolidPenta, SolidTetra).
SolidPropHyperelastic: The property of a fully nonlinear hyperelastic solid element.
SolidPropNonlinear: The nonlinear extension of the SolidProp with the same property ID, for the solid elements (SolidHexa, SolidPenta, SolidPyramid and SolidTetra) that name the SolidProp.
SolidPyramid: A solid with four corners on a quadrilateral base, one apex and up to eight additional edge nodes.
SolidTetra: A tetrahedral solid with four corner nodes and up to six additional nodes on its edges. The position of an edge-node ID in the record determines which edge it belongs to.
SphereShape: Defines a spherical region used to select Eulerian elements for initial conditions or body forces.
SphericalDetonation: Stores the spherical source definition referenced by an explicit material model.
SphericalFrame1: One spherical coordinate system defined by three grid points.
SphericalFrame2: A spherical coordinate system defined by three points.
SpotweldJoinPairs: Pairs of grid points of one-dimensional or shell elements that are joined (a spotweld) until the failure criterion of the pair is met.
